mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for ≥ 4 consecutive months, or inflation proxies (CPIAUCSL) show no acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 jobs while unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 4% simultaneously predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength boosts corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline of neutral labor conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by ≥ 2% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening domestic demand and reduced corporate earnings momentum.
regime_hint: Early stage of economic soft landing turning into contraction
failure_condition: No significant negative return in 20 days despite sustained weakness in INDPRO (p-value > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly drop in housing starts (HOUST) by 10% or more predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects contracting construction activity and downstream demand compression.
regime_hint: Early signs of a housing contraction
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive in > 60% of such HOUST declines (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4% while UNRATE remains above 5%, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as expectations of future rate cuts boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days when FEDFUNDS[3mo] remains below 4% for > 3 months without a subsequent UNRATE decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market disorganization and reduced business hiring confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such PAYEMS spikes versus a neutral baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) inflation rate exceeding 0.3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects expectations of future rate cuts and equity revaluation.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return in 70% of such CPIAUCSL inflation spikes (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit monthly decline in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to GDP deflator proxy via INDPRO inversion) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weak consumer demand and supply-side constraints.
regime_hint: Indirect evidence of consumer demand weakness
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative 60-day forward return when INDPRO shows only mild declines (p > 0.05).
